blocks.html: First-Person View drops your camera to ground level so you can scout terrain, sightlines and cover the way you would actually see them on the ground.

slides.title: Open the First-Person tool
slides.html: Open the First-Person tool from the Additional Tools and Settings menu. It places buttons at the top of the map and two soft joysticks on the right and left.

slides.title: Enable and pick your viewpoint
slides.html: Tap the First-Person View button, then tap the spot on the map you want to look from.

slides.title: Move and tilt the camera
slides.html: Use the right joystick to scout. It toggles between DRIVE to move and TILT to angle the camera.

slides.title: Adjust your elevation
slides.html: Use the left joystick to raise or lower your eye level. Elevation goes above ground level and below ground for a subterranean view.

slides.title: Exit First-Person View
slides.html: Tap the First-Person icon again to leave the perspective and return to the default overhead map view.
